rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296393400000000}What do you mean, enemies?
There shouldn't be anyone for us to fight.

{C:81930600}{C:819582963A3400000000}Calm down!
You're a man! Don't panic!

{C:81930100}{C:819582963B3400000000}Dad?

{C:81930600}{C:819582963C3400000000}Good, you can hear me?
Without a ship,
we can't get to you.

{C:819582963D3400000000}I'll give you instructions from the ground.
Just do what you can to hold out.

{C:81930300}{C:819582963E3400000000}No way...
We can't do this, Dad!

{C:81930600}{C:819582963F3400000000}It's all right. You two can do it.
I'll give you a brief explanation of combat.

{C:81958296403400000000}If you fight as I explain, at least
we should be able to keep the city from harm.
Please, do your best.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296413400000000}Okay, I'll try!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296423400000000}First, calm down and look at the top of the monitor.

{C:81958296433400000000}You should see data labeled HP and EN
up there.
Do you see it?

{C:81930100}{C:81958296443400000000}The top of the screen? ...Oh, this?
I found it, Dad.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296453400000000}Good. I'll explain HP first.
This {C:819782830400}HP{C:819782830000} reading
shows the Norstan's durability.

{C:81958296463400000000}In other words,
when the Norstan's HP reaches zero,
we lose--

{C:81958296473400000000}Conversely,
we win by reducing the enemy's HP to zero.
...Do you understand?

{C:81930100}{C:81958296483400000000}Yeah.
Basically, before the Norstan runs out of HP,

{C:81958296493400000000}we just have to get their ship's HP
down to zero, right?

{C:81930600}{C:819582964A3400000000}Exactly.

{C:819582964B3400000000}Next is the {C:819782830400}EN{C:819782830000} reading.
This value
shows the Norstan's energy.

{C:819582964C3400000000}Whenever the ship takes action,
such as deploying a unit,
it almost always consumes EN.

{C:819582964D3400000000}If you run short of EN in a crisis,
it could get you killed in the worst case.
Never waste it.

{C:819582964E3400000000}Now, I'll explain attacking.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582964F3400000000}In combat, both sides take turns.
Each turn is divided into a defense phase
and an attack phase.

{C:81958296503400000000}We attack, and the enemy defends.
The enemy attacks, and we defend.
Combat consists of repeating this cycle.

{C:81958296513400000000}Since we have the initiative,
this battle begins with the attack phase
of our turn.

{C:81958296523400000000}Now,
I'll explain the battlefield.

{C:81958296533400000000}The places where units can deploy are marked
by {C:819782830400}lanes{C:819782830000} connecting our side to the enemy's.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296543400000000}There are six lanes.
Deployed units take up space
according to their width.

{C:81958296553400000000}For FT and GT units,
the standard unit width is two.

{C:81958296563400000000}Therefore,
a maximum of three machines
can stand side by side.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296583400000000}So there's a front and a back?
What's the difference?

{C:81930600}{C:81958296593400000000}The drawback of the Forward position is
that it's easier to take damage,
but it also makes attacking easier.

{C:819582965A3400000000}Conversely, the Back position makes it
harder to take damage,
but it also makes attacking harder.

{C:819582965B3400000000}Choose the more suitable position
based on the enemy's situation
and the units you can deploy.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582965F3400000000}When a unit runs out of HP, it is damaged.
It can't deploy from the ship
until it receives the minimum repairs.

{C:81958296603400000000}However, units are repaired
every turn.

{C:81958296613400000000}If several units have been destroyed,
you can't choose which one
will be repaired that turn.

{C:81958296623400000000}To fight reliably,
try to avoid having units damaged
as much as possible.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296633400000000}Okay, I'll try.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296643400000000}As for EN,
you can basically think of it
just as you would a ship's.

{C:81958296653400000000}Next are unit attributes.

{C:81958296663400000000}First, units have location attributes: 
{C:819782830400}Ground{C:819782830000}, {C:819782830400}Anti-Air{C:819782830000}, and {C:819782830400}Flying{C:819782830000}.
These indicate their position.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296683400000000}And GT-A
has the Ground location attribute.

{C:81958296693400000000}When units have the same location attribute,
there's no change, but...

{C:819582966A3400000000}when units with different attributes
fight, the effect is substantial.

{C:819582966B3400000000}Basically, Ground has an advantage over Anti-Air,
Flying has an advantage over Ground,
and Ground has an advantage over Anti-Air.

{C:819582966C3400000000}Remembering this three-way relationship
should prove useful.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582966D3400000000}Next, I'll explain another attribute.

{C:819582966E3400000000}Each unit has a range
at which it can attack.

{C:819582966F3400000000}{C:819782830400}Long Range{C:819782830000}, {C:819782830400}Short Range{C:819782830000},
and there are also 
{C:819782830400}Piercing units{C:819782830000} that attack at both short and long range simultaneously.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296713400000000}And Short Range attack units
like GT-A
are probably better suited to the front.

{C:81958296723400000000}These Short Range, Long Range and Piercing types are called 
{C:819782830400}range attributes{C:819782830000}.
Make sure you remember them.

{C:81958296733400000000}Now, I'll get back to explaining the combat procedure.

{C:81958296743400000000}You need to give action orders
to the units you've deployed.


{x00}

unless you give them orders like this.
Don't forget.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296763400000000}Giving a unit an action order
consumes that unit's EN.

{C:81958296773400000000}Like the ship, it can't move if it runs short of EN,
so be careful.

{C:81958296783400000000}Once you've finished all actions and orders,
select Turn End,
and your units will advance on the enemy.


{x00}

{C:81930C00}{C:819582967A3400000000}So they're receiving instructions from the ground.
An opponent with no combat experience at all...
They pose no problem.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582967C3400000000}The enemy unit
seems to have chosen to defend.

{C:819582967D3400000000}An enemy that chooses to defend
can spend its defense power
to reduce our attack power.

{C:819582967E3400000000}What's more, that defense power value
only applies for one turn,
and is fully restored the next turn.

{C:819582967F3400000000}But that also means its defense power
doesn't recover during the turn.
It only decreases with each attack it takes.

{C:81958296803400000000}If we can deplete its defense power
all the way to zero,
we'll be able to damage it.

{C:81958296813400000000}Against a defending enemy, what matters is
whether you can attack with enough power
to exceed its defense within a single turn.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296833400000000}Units act in order,
starting with the fastest.

{C:81958296843400000000}Basically, units taking action
advance toward the enemy ship
in order to attack it.

{C:81958296853400000000}And when units from both sides
are in the same lane,
they fight.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296863400000000}As I thought, a defending unit
isn't easy to take down...

{C:81930100}{C:81958296873400000000}Damn it.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296883400000000}...But GT-B is next.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296893400000000}Huh?

{C:81930600}{C:819582968A3400000000}As I'm sure you know,
GT-B is a Long Range unit.

{C:819582968B3400000000}Normally, when other Ground units
are in the same lane, you can't pass them,
whether they're allies or enemies.

{C:819582968C3400000000}But GT-B, a Long Range unit,
can attack one space farther
than the normal attack range.

{C:819582968D3400000000}In other words, it can attack
the enemy in front of GT-A.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582968E3400000000}By using Long Range
and Short Range units this way,
you can attack in succession.

{C:81930100}{C:819582968F3400000000}Oh, I get it.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296903400000000}However!
There's something you must watch out for
when planning successive attacks.

{C:81958296913400000000}Even if, as before,
you put a Short Range unit in Forward
and a Long Range unit in Back,

{C:81958296923400000000}if the Short Range unit in Forward
is slower than the Long Range unit
you've placed in Back,

{C:81958296933400000000}the Long Range unit can't advance,
and its turn will end
before it reaches the enemy's position.

{C:81958296943400000000}Speed can easily lead to mistakes
in various other situations as well.
...Be careful.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930C00}{C:81958296953400000000}For a first battle,
they're doing rather well...


{C:81930100}{C:81958296963400000000}Dad, it looks like they're going to attack.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296973400000000}Don't panic!
First, take a good look around
and understand the situation.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296983400000000}I got it!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296993400000000}Listen. When you switch from defense to attack,
ships and units recover.

{C:819582969A3400000000}Specifically,
ships and units replenish their EN.

{C:819582969B3400000000}And units aboard ships
recover
their HP.

{C:819582969C3400000000}What's more, one damaged unit
finishes its repairs and can deploy again.



{x00}

{C:81930100}{C:819582969D3400000000}What?
That unit's back in action?!

{C:81930600}{C:819582969E3400000000}Relax. It may be repaired,
but its HP shouldn't have recovered yet.
Even if it deploys now, it's no match for us.

{C:819582969F3400000000}More importantly...
it looks like another unit is coming.


{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296A13400000000}That one in the back...
Didn't it just change lanes?

{C:81930600}{C:81958296A23400000000}Yes, it definitely moved.
...Right.
I'd better explain that too.

{C:81958296A33400000000}Deployed units can spend EN
to move to an adjacent lane,
or to Forward or Back.

{C:81958296A43400000000}Of course, a unit can't move if its action
has already been decided, or if other units
surround it and leave it no room to move.

that you don't advance when attacking.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296AD3400000000}Whoa!

{C:81958296AE3400000000}Dad!
Even if I have the advantage,
I can't take on two units!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296B03400000000}Don't panic. Listen carefully!

{C:81958296B13400000000}When fighting several units,
attack power, defense power and damage
are distributed according to the area of contact across their widths.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296B53400000000}That example
was about the damage our side takes.

{C:81958296B63400000000}Conversely, consider our attacks.
Each of them has to fight GT-A,
and on top of that...

{C:81958296B73400000000}each has to take half
of Impulse 7's attack.

{C:81958296B83400000000}Do you understand?
Then get out there!
